methodological_rigor.justification: Single-center retrospective cohort of 604 cN0 PTC patients with 7:3 train/validation split, five machine-learning models across five feature groups, LASSO feature selection, Optuna hyperparameter tuning, and 5-fold CV. The design is thorough, but there is no external/held-out multicenter test set, only an internal validation split, and class imbalance is acknowledged to drive low sensitivity (recall 0.36 for CLNM, 0.35 for LNM) despite high AUC. Manual ROI segmentation by a single sonographer without ICC, JPEG (lossy) images across three US systems without harmonization, and qualitative CEUS without TIC quantification are all acknowledged as weaknesses that could substantially affect feature robustness.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Retrospective prediction-model development with internal validation corresponds to Oxford LoE 2b. Accurate prediction of CLNM/LNM in cN0 PTC has high clinical relevance for avoiding unnecessary prophylactic central lymph node dissection, but the reported low sensitivity and absence of external validation make the current model not yet clinically deployable.

reporting_quality.justification: TRIPOD is the applicable standard for prediction model development. The manuscript reports predictors, outcome, handling of continuous variables, model types, tuning procedure, and multiple performance metrics (AUC, PR, Brier, calibration, DCA, SHAP). Missing TRIPOD items include a participant flow diagram, predictor definitions with measurement reliability (no ICC), prespecified performance targets, explicit handling of class imbalance, and formal calibration intercept/slope. No data/code availability statement despite using public tools.

novelty_literature.justification: Radiomics models combining ultrasound and clinical features to predict PTC lymph node metastasis have been reported (Liu 2019, Li 2020, Jin 2022, Tang 2025). The novelty here is explicit integration of CEUS-derived radiomics features plus discrete contrast parameters within a RF framework and comparison across five feature groups and five ML models. This is a meaningful extension but within a crowded radiomics literature.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is organized and reasonably clear with comprehensive figure descriptions (ROC, PR, DCA, calibration, SHAP, LASSO paths). Some issues include run-on feature lists, minor grammatical issues, duplicated phrases ('bilateral pCND followed by personalized radioiodine... bilateral prophylactic central lymph node dissection(pCND) followed by personalized radioiodine therapy'), and Table 1 description not matching its stated content (training/testing set univariate analysis). Overall readable but could be tightened.

key_strengths: Integrates clinical features, conventional US radiomics, CEUS-derived radiomics, and CEUS contrast parameters
Systematic comparison of five ML models across five feature groups with LASSO selection and Optuna tuning
SHAP interpretability and multi-metric evaluation (AUC, PR, Brier, calibration, DCA)
Authors transparently acknowledge major limitations (JPEG compression, multi-vendor, single reader, low sensitivity)
key_concerns: Single-center retrospective design without external validation
Low sensitivity (~0.35) despite high AUC, limiting clinical utility for rule-out decisions
Manual ROI delineation by a single sonographer without ICC or inter-rater analysis
Lossy JPEG images across three US systems without harmonization likely compromise radiomic feature robustness
Incomplete TRIPOD reporting (flow diagram, calibration intercept/slope, prespecified targets); no data/code availability
chief_reviewer.rationale: A methodologically thorough but exploratory radiomics study with candid acknowledgment of significant technical limitations; suitable for a mid-tier oncology/radiology journal after external validation and TRIPOD-aligned reporting improvements.
